images.description: A design-statement collage on a cream ground. Down the centre, three stacked hand-drawn elements between dotted vertical guide lines: a flat disc with a central circular opening (cut off at the top edge), a cutaway axonometric of a ring-shaped building with radial rooms around a central circular void, and a second cutaway axonometric with tiered seating in the centre (cut off at the bottom edge). Bands of flowing parallel lines sweep down the left side and pass under the rings, ending in a musical note. A column of design-statement body text at the top left is truncated at the left margin and top. To the right sit the heading DESIGN STATEMENT over a faded, ghosted drawing of concentric arcs subdivided into cells with dimension-style marks, a collaged vignette of a pianist and dancing couple on a music staff with a torn-paper edge, and fragments of handwritten-style sheet music at the bottom right.
images.thirdPartyNotes: The pianist-and-dancing-couple vignette has the look of a reproduced vintage illustration pasted in on a torn-paper element and is treated as third-party. The sheet-music fragments beneath the vignette and at the bottom right (treble and bass staves with notes on aged paper) appear to be reproduced notation and are also treated as third-party. The faded drawing of concentric arcs behind the heading is of uncertain origin, possibly a reproduced technical drawing used as a background texture, and is not cropped. The roof disc, the two cutaway axonometrics, the flow lines and the musical note are consistent with the author's own hand drawing.

images.description: Mixed-media site-analysis collage. A sketched line map of streets and building footprints, with the site plot shaded red, a blue-grey canal band and red dashed arrows tracing routes, is layered with four photographs of graffiti-covered walls along the top, sepia-toned photographic cut-outs of walking pedestrians, two inset black-and-white photographs of water flowing past a lock or weir, a photographic water and vegetation texture in the lower right, and tall layered wave-like line drawings in grey, orange and red along the left. A column of first-person reflective text runs vertically beside the waves.
images.thirdPartyNotes: The graffiti pieces in the four wall photographs are other artists' work and the photographer is not identified; the pedestrian cut-outs read as stock photographic cut-outs; the two inset black-and-white photographs look like found aerial or archive imagery; the lower-right water and vegetation texture is also photographic and of unknown source. The line map, red plot, dashed movement lines and wave drawings read as Tala's own. The whole collage should be shown only if the photographs and cut-outs are confirmed as Tala's own or licensed.
images.textVisible: Vertical text column, cut off at the top edge of the image: "The graffiti surrounding the site strongly influenced my artistic approach to site analysis. I became fascinated by the raw c[...] colour, layering, and expression embedded within the site. Speaks volumes, a reflection of movement, identity, and comm[...] Alongside this, I was drawn to the rhythm and flow of the canal itself — the movement of runners, cyclists, pedestrians, an[...] created a continuous choreography across the site. I also explored surrounding sounds and voice waves, which began inf[...] my drawings and collages. Through this process, the site analysis evolved into a story about rhythm, circulation, creativity, dance, and movement within the urban landscape." Graffiti tags are partly legible (e.g. "NEDS", "I NEED MONEY"). The text reads as finished reflective prose rather than production notes, but it is truncated by the source crop and one sentence lacks a subject ("Speaks volumes").

images.description: Composite board from the Material / Assembly / Technical Study spread. It combines two published interior photographs of the ABBA Arena (a pink-lit timber lattice roof, and bolted glulam columns beside a timber-clad kiosk with a grey fluted panel), a clipped heading reading ABBA STADIUM STRATFORD / MATERIAL REUSE, two columns of explanatory text, and a two-by-two grid of photographs of Tala's own timber model of a branching column, cut from thin plywood with dark cut edges and etched joint markings.
images.thirdPartyNotes: The two large interior photographs (top-left, pink-lit lattice ceiling; bottom-centre, bolted glulam columns and slatted kiosk) are published photographs of the ABBA Arena in Stratford, not Tala's own work. They must not be republished on the website without permission and photographer credit. The four model photographs in the top-right grid are Tala's own.
images.textVisible: Heading (top line clipped): 'ABBA STADIUM STRATFORD' / 'MATERIAL REUSE'. Left column: 'Reclaimed glulam timber from the existing ABBA Arena structure after its lifespan, extending the life of the material rather than demolishing and discarding it' / 'The ABBA Arena uses a branching timber structural system made of' (cut off at bottom). Right column (cut off at right edge): 'I reinterpret this structure within my design through sloping timb[er] beams, exposed connections, and rhythmic structural intersectio[ns] that resemble musical notation and sound waves' / 'The reclaimed timber is reused as primary structural elements including roof beams, columns, and internal framing systems' / 'Exposed steel plates and bolts celebrate the construction proces[s] rather than hiding it, creating a more haptic and expressive architectural language' / 'Reusing the ABBA timber also reduces embodied carbon and supports circular construction principles through material reuse a[nd] adaptation' / 'The reused structure creates a connection between two' (cut off). The text reads as finished narrative rather than draft notes, but it is clipped at the top, right and bottom edges of the extracted image.
